lede: Nonprofit Megaphone leads its category wearing the category's most common outfit: an electric-blue template shared with three direct competitors. Each direction below keeps the proof and gives it a look of its own. Every mockup is live HTML at desktop and phone width.

why.title: The site today
bullets: One exit everywhere, "Book a Free Call", under seven different labels
No pricing, no eligibility check, nothing a board can forward
The proof is real but scattered: 780+ clients, $48M+ managed, Google's own endorsement

why.title: Who is buying
bullets: Tired executive and communications directors; burnout is up sharply in 2026
Their concrete fear is losing the grant to Google's 5% click-through rule
They research before they call and reward calm competence over hype

why.title: The white space
bullets: Electric-blue SaaS is the most crowded look in the category
Nobody owns proof-as-document, warm editorial, or a signal red
One direction keeps the blue, so evolution versus rupture is a real choice
The megaphone's own geometry: vermilion arcs, rays and level bars on warm paper
Proof pinned to the diagram: a named lead at the origin, dated outcomes on the arcs
Google's 5% floor drawn as the innermost ring, so the risk is visible up front
Amplitude.rightFor: A leadership team that wants an ownable rebrand and will lock the design tokens in Webflow.
Amplitude.accent: Vermilion, brand blue at the origin
Amplitude.oneLiner: The megaphone's own geometry as a live proof diagram on warm paper.

bullets: The publication of record: newsprint white, black ink, one deep blue
An "on the record" ledger with dated, sourced figures and a real chart
Lowest-risk register; reads as a sharpening to 780 existing clients
Broadsheet.rightFor: A team that wants institutional authority, will publish pricing and dated figures, and prefers the safest register.
Broadsheet.oneLiner: The publication of record: newsprint, black ink, one deep blue.

bullets: Civic infrastructure: pure white, flat blue blocks, a signal-red button, one typeface
The hero is a grant account record with Google's four rules checked off
Plain language and accessibility as the aesthetic; an audit, not an ad
Public_Works.rightFor: A team selling to boards and compliance-minded directors that puts clarity ahead of styling.
needs: Consent for a real account record
Public_Works.accent: Civic blue blocks, signal red CTA
Public_Works.oneLiner: Civic infrastructure in pure white, flat blue and a signal red.

bullets: Keeps the electric blue on purpose, as one big bordered stage
Proof staged as physical objects: a dashboard card, stickers, a highlighter
The evolutionary option: same identity, far better execution
Full_Volume.rightFor: A team that will not retire the blue for its clients and wants the execution fixed, not the identity replaced.
needs: Client consent for the card's figures
Full_Volume.oneLiner: The electric blue kept, and turned from a wall into a stage.

bullets: Linen, forest green and ochre with Fraunces italic; the warmest of the set
The hero is a photographed account lead beside the one sentence they sign each month
People-first: the team is the product, shown plainly
Signed_Sentence.rightFor: A team whose strongest asset is its people and that will fund a photo shoot and a monthly signed note.
needs: Commit to a monthly signed note
Signed_Sentence.oneLiner: The people who run your grant, and the sentence they sign each month.

Poster.ground: White page, mustard and teal fields

Sky.accent: Clear blue CTA, one sun dot
Sky.device: Floating chips on a rising line

Atlas.ground: Pale steel blue-gray with map tints

recommendation.name: Amplitude
bullets: The only signature grown from the brand's own mark, so it is ownable
Carries the full proof layer while staying calm enough for a tired buyer
Ships static-first in CSS and inline SVG; motion is optional

runnerUp.name: Broadsheet
bullets: Lowest risk and easiest to approve; reads as sharpening, not rupture
The most honest evidence object in the set
Cheapest to build well in Webflow, but the least ownable

evidence: A signed one-sentence monthly note from a named account lead
The guarantee is a person: Amber Snow, $25, a direct email
Every figure dated, from one canonical numbers sheet
Google's 5% floor drawn and explained wherever a chart appears
A rep-free "Am I eligible?" check with an honest no
A flat monthly fee stated; a range if leadership approves
decisions: Keep, evolve or retire the blue?
Fund a motion sprint or ship static?
notYet: Everything beyond the homepage: 716 URLs, 618 undated posts, 54 case studies
The booking flow: seven CTA labels and an unstyled calendar embed
Timeline and budget, which depend on the direction chosen

The_Ledger.why: Statement-as-hero; absorbed by Broadsheet and Public Works.

Charter.why: Heritage navy and gold; reads as a law firm.

Signal_Room.why: Dark dashboard; lowest score with the nonprofit buyer.
